capabilities.title: Appearance, locale, and date/time/time-zone
capabilities.contract: General Settings persists a System, Light, or Dark appearance preference; the shared resolver maps System to the current device appearance for visual application. It also supports the Interface locale, device-local or explicit IANA time zones, device-local date and time formatting, and explicit date and time formats. Revision History honors saved formatting while generated supporting UI text uses the Interface locale independently of Article language.

capabilities.title: Optional packaged-app telemetry consent
capabilities.contract: During public beta, the packaged Electron app shows a localized, keyboard-accessible default-on switch for a finite pseudonymous diagnostic and usage event contract, plus an enabled-only copyable Telemetry ID for deletion requests. The server emits one finite terminal event after persisted Assistant or direct Editorial completion, or after their failure/cancellation; staged Assistant work is not counted separately. The workspace batches only actual Draft save/discard persistence attempts that began with telemetry enabled into a 30-second in-memory aggregate; no-op checkpoints are excluded. Electron emits one terminal event for each manual, deletion-protective, restore-recovery, or update-recovery SQLite snapshot. Native backup restores emit only after the restored application completes startup or fails/rolls back; Article revision restores emit only after persistence completes or fails. Main validates each IPC request and event, keeps identity and consent outside Article data, clears both on opt-out, and treats missing delivery configuration as disabled. Browser and development runtimes cannot send telemetry.
capabilities.persistence: Electron userData/runtime-settings.json only; it is excluded from SQLite Article data, backups, and restore staging.
limitations: A manually inspected opted-in packaged-beta deletion request, payload, dashboard definitions, and packaged Windows acceptance remain release prerequisites.

capabilities.title: Configurable application shortcuts
capabilities.contract: Settings can persist command overrides and expose conflict-aware shortcut configuration. The Editorial Assistant also supports choosing Enter or Ctrl+Enter as the send key independently of command overrides.
limitations: Complete workspace-action wiring remains tracked separately.

capabilities.title: AI connections and activation
capabilities.contract: Authors choose OpenAI, OpenCode Zen, Anthropic, Google Gemini API, xAI Grok, or DeepSeek before adding an environment-variable connection. In Electron, they first choose an environment variable or managed API key, which Skladno verifies then stores in Windows Credential Manager. Connections are active by default; authors can activate or deactivate each one independently, rename it, test it, or confirm deletion without exposing secret values.

capabilities.title: Default, supporting-text, per-skill, reasoning, and favorite-model preferences
capabilities.contract: Each selected model records its active connection as well as its provider model ID, so duplicate model names remain routable and an OpenCode Zen model can disclose its underlying vendor. Default, supporting-text, per-skill, reasoning, and favorite-model preferences apply globally. An optional text-generation model handles supporting text such as Proposal summaries and falls back to the default. Authors can save favorite available models, search the available list, and filter it by recognized vendor. Low, medium, and high reasoning-level controls are offered only for selected OpenAI models. Presentation receives Settings through the application service, persistence uses focused repositories, and legacy preferences migrate to their formerly active connection without exposing unknown keys.

capabilities.title: Available model list refresh
capabilities.contract: Opening AI Settings loads the current model lists for every active OpenAI, OpenCode Zen, Anthropic, Google Gemini API, xAI Grok, or DeepSeek connection; authors can refresh them again to retry or retrieve provider changes. Each returned model retains the connection that supplied it. The OpenAI catalog admits only the gpt-5.5 and gpt-5.6 model families; Zen retains its complete returned catalog. A refreshed list is not proof that every Editorial Operation is supported.
capabilities.persistence: Server-side provider refresh only; the resulting list is not persisted.

capabilities.title: Publishing profiles and language defaults
capabilities.contract: Default, No restrictions, LinkedIn Post, LinkedIn Article, and named custom non-negative limits provide guidance; the selected default applies to new Articles while Articles retain independent selection. Custom profiles have stable IDs, appear before add controls, and require confirmed removal; removing the selected default resets to Default. Settings persists one default Article language and deduplicated translation languages excluding it. Translate creates reviewable proposals for every configured target.

capabilities.title: Browser-selected backup folder, schedule, and retention
capabilities.contract: In supported web browsers, authors explicitly choose a local backup folder. The browser writes consistent SQLite snapshots there, lists compatible snapshots for explicit restore, and reloads after the loopback service safely replaces active data. Daily startup writes at most one automatic snapshot when the previously selected folder remains permitted, and retention removes only automatic snapshots.
capabilities.persistence: app_settings.application-backup-policy plus the browser's local folder permission handle; snapshots exclude environment variables and API keys.

capabilities.title: Explicit Electron local-data deletion
capabilities.contract: In Electron, an author can request deletion of the active resolved Skladno data directory through a no-argument native operation. The native confirmation explains the irreversible scope and always shows a Create a backup before deletion checkbox, checked only when a separate backup directory is configured. A requested backup must succeed before deletion continues. It cancels without changes, closes SQLite and background work before deletion, then exits only after successful removal. The renderer cannot supply a filesystem path.
capabilities.persistence: The confirmed active local data directory is removed. Installer and uninstaller behavior remains data-preserving.

capabilities.title: Explicit local-backup restoration
capabilities.contract: An author chooses a SQLite snapshot from the configured backup folder and explicitly confirms replacement. Browser restore uploads the selected snapshot only to the loopback service, which closes and reopens the local application before the browser reloads. Electron uses a staged native restart. The renderer cannot provide an active-data path. Skladno retains a recovery snapshot, validates the snapshot before and after replacement, and rolls back once when restored data cannot open.
capabilities.persistence: The selected snapshot replaces the active SQLite database only during restart. A private recovery snapshot remains outside the active database.

capabilities.title: Author-controlled unsigned Windows updates
capabilities.contract: About Settings asks the author in a confirmation dialog to allow GitHub update network access before any discovery request. After consent, it exposes automatic checks, a stable-only or prerelease-inclusive channel preference, explicit download, guarded restart, release notes, and recovery guidance. An available update appears in the Article Library utility area and opens About Settings with Updates focused. Browser builds omit the group; Electron development builds expose the persisted preferences but no discovery or download actions.
capabilities.persistence: The desktop runtime file stores the network-permission, automatic-check, and prerelease-channel preferences plus non-content update recovery metadata.

capabilities.title: Repository and license
capabilities.contract: About Settings provides compact external links to the GitHub source repository, issue tracker, and MIT License. It keeps these details read-only and opens links in the system browser.
capabilities.persistence: Static application metadata; no author data is stored.

scenarios.title: General time-zone preferences persist with accessible guidance
scenarios.event: The author selects an explicit IANA time zone or restores the system setting.
expected: The preference is saved with an accessible label, hint, and timestamp preview.
forbidden: Changing display preferences rewrites saved timestamps or Revision history.

scenarios.title: Telemetry remains installation-local and controllable
preconditions: The author opens General Settings in the Electron app.
scenarios.event: The author copies the Telemetry ID, then enables or disables diagnostic and usage data sharing.
expected: The main process confirms the persisted value before the switch changes.
The enabled-only Telemetry ID can be copied for a deletion request before opt-out clears it.
Each explicit Assistant or direct Editorial operation sends at most one finite terminal event, with no Article content.
Draft save/discard persistence attempts that started with telemetry enabled are emitted only as a bounded aggregate, with no Article content.
Electron snapshot creation emits one completed or failed finite backup event with no path or snapshot data.
Native backup and Article revision restoration emit one completed or failed recovery event only after their terminal outcome, with no Article content.
Opt-out clears the installation identity and future queued events.
forbidden: Copying consent or the Telemetry ID through Article backup or restore.

scenarios.title: Theme preference applies to the application shell
preconditions: The author has saved a System, Light, or Dark appearance preference.
scenarios.event: The application shell loads the preference or the device appearance changes while System is selected.
expected: Semantic UI tokens apply the selected appearance, and System follows the current device preference.
forbidden: Changing appearance modifies Article content or saved timestamps.

scenarios.title: Key-binding overrides remain conflict-aware
preconditions: The author configures an application shortcut.
scenarios.event: A key binding is normalized and checked against effective commands.
expected: The override can be persisted and conflicts are identified.
forbidden: An override silently replaces a conflicting command.

scenarios.title: AI connection metadata is managed without secrets
preconditions: The author is in the AI Settings section.
scenarios.event: The author adds, activates, deactivates, or confirms removal of a connection.
expected: Authors choose one of the six supported providers and an environment-variable or, in Electron, managed-credential method. Connections are active by default, may share an environment-variable name, and an API key can be verified and stored without being displayed or persisted in Skladno data.
forbidden: Displaying or persisting API key values.

scenarios.title: Model preferences resolve for editorial and supporting work
preconditions: A default model, text generation model, skill override, or reasoning effort is saved.
scenarios.event: A new editorial request is prepared.
expected: Editorial work resolves the built-in-skill override or default model through its saved active connection, while supporting text resolves its text-generation model or default-model fallback. Each selected OpenAI model receives its saved reasoning effort.

scenarios.title: Available models load automatically without becoming settings data
preconditions: At least one active AI connection is configured.
scenarios.event: The author opens AI Settings, changes an activation state, or manually refreshes the list.
expected: Every active connection's current model list is offered for selection with its supplying connection, without persisting the refreshed list as preference data.
forbidden: Persisting the refreshed list as a model preference.

scenarios.title: Publishing defaults survive reload
preconditions: The author selects a supported profile and may configure a custom name and non-negative limit.
scenarios.event: The service saves and reloads the profile default.
expected: The selected publishing profile, custom configuration, and language defaults are returned for new Articles and translation requests.

scenarios.title: Backups are recoverable without interrupting editing
preconditions: The author opens Data & backups Settings.
scenarios.event: The author chooses a backup folder, creates a manual backup, or the daily schedule runs at application startup.
expected: A consistent local SQLite snapshot is written through the browser permission handle and automatic retention leaves manual snapshots untouched.
forbidden: A backup failure interrupts Article editing or exposes environment-variable secrets.

scenarios.title: Update controls require author action
preconditions: A packaged Windows release exposes an available update.
scenarios.event: The author opens About Settings, allows update network access, and checks for updates.
expected: The network-permission, automatic-check, and prerelease-channel switches are accessible, a confirmation dialog precedes the persisted network permission, no discovery request occurs before consent, Download appears only after explicit discovery, and the status shows while the update downloads.
forbidden: A browser or development build exposes update controls, an update-discovery request occurs without consent, or a download starts automatically.

scenarios.title: Explicit local-data deletion is contained and backup-gated
preconditions: The author uses the Electron Data & backups Settings section with a resolved local data directory.
scenarios.event: The author cancels deletion, deletes after a native confirmation, or selects backup and deletion.
expected: Cancellation leaves the data unchanged.
A requested backup must complete and be non-empty before deletion proceeds.
Only the active resolved Skladno data directory is deleted after background work and SQLite close, and Skladno exits after success.
forbidden: Deleting an unresolved or broad path.
Continuing to deletion after backup failure.
Deleting local author data during ordinary uninstall.

scenarios.title: Backup restoration is staged and recoverable
preconditions: The author has configured a backup folder containing a Skladno SQLite snapshot.
scenarios.event: The author selects a backup and confirms restoration.
expected: Cancellation leaves active data unchanged.

Skladno validates the selected snapshot, retains a recovery snapshot, and opens the restored Articles, Revisions, Draft checkpoints, Assistant history, style data, and Settings after restart or browser reload.
If restored startup fails, Skladno rolls back to the recovery snapshot once.
forbidden: The renderer supplies an active-data path.
An invalid or incompatible snapshot replaces active data.
Skladno claims success after a failed replacement or rollback.
